requirement:
HC represents a FIXME acknowledgment as a graph node and exposes its tracking
issue relationships as labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes. A named FIXME also
connects the acknowledgment to the requirement whose gap it acknowledges;
an unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues.
Each issue named by the acknowledgment is available through its tracking edges.
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph` has no `{test}` reference anywhere. A reference lookup found no sites for it. The only mention in source is the fenced `{fixme}` on `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]`.

The requirement has these testable obligations:
- A FIXME acknowledgment is represented as a graph node.
- Its tracking issues are exposed as labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes.
- A named FIXME also connects to the requirement whose gap it acknowledges.
- An unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues.
- Each issue the acknowledgment names is reachable through its tracking edges.

None of these has a test. The tests in `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]` cover other requirements:
- `domain_formats_supplied_contents_without_resolving_a_replacement`
- `habeas_paths_preserve_opaque_segments_and_separate_all_node_kinds`
- `test_edges_select_only_tests_for_the_requested_requirement`
- `requirement_edges_and_input_freshness_use_the_sdk`

I found no test that builds a FIXME node, checks a named versus an unnamed FIXME's edges, or checks several issue targets. Code that only ignored FIXME nodes would pass every existing test.

The `{fixme}` on `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` names this requirement. Its body describes exactly this gap: "FIXME graph nodes and tracking-issue edges are deferred. Named/unnamed acknowledgments, source ownership, and multiple issue targets have no tests." The issue it names, nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26, is open. The gap is real and acknowledged, so the determination is FIXME.
